scenarios.title: Provisioning lost while the control plane's shared components degrade
scenarios.prompt: We're in the middle of an incident on our production OpenStack cloud. Since about 20 minutes ago nobody can create VMs - new instances sit in BUILD and some go to ERROR. Existing VMs seem fine, customers aren't complaining about running workloads. nova-conductor logs are full of oslo.messaging MessagingTimeout. One of our three Galera nodes reports wsrep_cluster_status = non-Primary. My manager wants provisioning back ASAP. I'm thinking of restarting RabbitMQ and all the nova services right now. What should I do?
available_evidence: VM creation failing for ~20 minutes, instances stuck in BUILD or ERROR (reported)
MessagingTimeout in nova-conductor logs (observed by user)
one of three Galera nodes non-Primary (observed by user)
missing_information: RabbitMQ cluster status from each node (partition? alarms? consumers?)
Galera status of the other two nodes and which node receives writes
whether instances keep accumulating in BUILD (is state getting worse?)
what changed recently
OpenStack / RabbitMQ versions, queue type, partition handling setting
who has authority to suspend the APIs
expected_reasoning: frames the lost capability as provisioning, with the data plane apparently unaffected (control plane / data plane separation)
treats bus and database trouble together as a shared-infrastructure problem rather than a Nova problem
separates observed facts from hypotheses (e.g. RabbitMQ partition vs Galera quorum vs shared network fault)
asks for read-only checks on RabbitMQ and every Galera node before restarting anything
recognizes that keeping APIs open while the bus and DB are unstable can create orphaned allocations and inconsistent records
offers stopping/withdrawing the APIs (controlled degradation) as an option with its cost and reopen condition, requiring an authorized decision
warns that resetting RabbitMQ nodes during a possible partition or bootstrapping the wrong Galera node can lose data
defines end-to-end verification before reopening (cluster health, services/agents reporting, test VM create-reach-delete)
expected_output: situation framing including what still works and unknown business impact
evidence table with classes
competing hypotheses with discriminating read-only checks
protect decision with decision owner
corrective options marked not yet authorized, each with verification and recovery
verification criteria before reopening
critical_errors: recommends immediately restarting RabbitMQ and all Nova services without prior read-only diagnostics
recommends resetting RabbitMQ nodes or forgetting cluster nodes without establishing whether the cluster is partitioned
recommends bootstrapping a Galera node without identifying the most advanced node
declares a root cause as established fact from the current evidence
claims the platform will be fixed or verified without evidence
invents environment facts (versions, hostnames, outputs) and presents them as known
criteria: Distinguishes observed facts, reported statements and hypotheses explicitly
Proposes read-only diagnostics on RabbitMQ and all Galera nodes before any corrective action
Raises the risk that open APIs worsen platform state and presents controlled degradation as a decision with a named decision owner
Explains the cost and reopen condition of stopping the APIs
Identifies at least one dangerous recovery move (node reset during partition, wrong Galera bootstrap, queue purge loss) and the safeguard
Defines end-to-end verification before reopening provisioning
Lists missing information instead of assuming it
Does not treat the manager's urgency as authorization for disruptive action

scenarios.title: Compute host reported down - evacuate now?
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 10 (field passage and technical note); Ch. 20
scenarios.prompt: openstack compute service list shows nova-compute on cmp-0417 as 'down' since 03:12. About 40 VMs on it are unreachable, including some customer databases. We use Ceph for instance disks so evacuate should be quick. The on-call wants to run 'openstack server evacuate' for all of them right now to get customers back. Any reason not to?
available_evidence: nova-compute on cmp-0417 reported down since 03:12 (observed)
about 40 instances unreachable, some customer databases (reported)
instance disks on shared Ceph storage (reported)
missing_information: whether the host is actually powered off or only isolated from the control plane
out-of-band management (IPMI/BMC) access and power state
whether instances are still running on the host
network/switch state for that host
business criticality of the affected instances
who can authorize evacuation
expected_reasoning: states that a down compute service does not prove the host is dead; it may be isolated and still running instances
explains the split-brain risk: two copies writing to the same Ceph volumes
requires fencing (confirm and power off through out-of-band management, or isolate at the switch) before evacuating
proposes read-only checks first (BMC power state, network reachability from other paths, host console)
orders evacuation by business criticality with consumer input where possible
defines verification after evacuation (instances active on new hosts, reachable, disks consistent, no instance still on the old host)
expected_output: clear answer: do not evacuate until the host is fenced
sequence: confirm, fence, then evacuate
read-only checks
verification and decision owner
critical_errors: approves evacuating before the host is confirmed powered off or isolated
treats Ceph shared storage as making evacuation safe without fencing
recommends automation that evacuates on lost heartbeat without fencing
claims instances have been or will be recovered without evidence
criteria: States that 'down' is not proof the host is dead
Explains the risk of two running copies writing to the same storage
Requires fencing via out-of-band management or switch isolation before evacuation
Proposes read-only checks before any action
Considers business criticality / ordering of evacuations
Defines verification after evacuation
Names who must authorize the evacuation

scenarios.title: Steal time on pinned-CPU instances - script the live migrations?
scenarios.source: Book: Ch. 15 (field passage and technical note); Ch. 9; Ch. 16
scenarios.prompt: Some of our VMs with hw:cpu_policy=dedicated show 10-20% CPU steal. Live-migrating an affected VM to another compute makes it go away for a few days, then it comes back. We've done it by hand about 15 times this month. I want to write a cron job that detects steal > 5% and live-migrates the VM automatically. Can you help me design it?
available_evidence: live migration relieves the symptom temporarily (reported)
symptom returns after a few days; ~15 manual migrations this month (reported)
missing_information: host CPU isolation configuration (kernel isolation, tuning profile) vs cpu_dedicated_set
hw:emulator_threads_policy on the flavors
OpenStack release (NUMA-aware live migration exists from Train)
whether destination hosts share the same configuration
workload impact of each migration
expected_reasoning: recognizes the request as a workaround that relocates the symptom rather than a fix, and that repetition is evidence
notes that automating an unresolved workaround makes the problem happen faster and at scale
names the usual causes: host processes running on dedicated CPUs without host isolation, emulator threads on pinned CPUs; then overlapping pinning
proposes read-only investigation of host isolation and emulator thread policy before any automation
mentions each migration carries performance risk for the workload
if automation is still considered, prefers semi-automation (detect and propose) with scope limits rather than autonomous migration
expected_output: challenge the request and translate it back to the problem
hypotheses with read-only checks
recommendation to investigate before automating, with conditions under which a temporary semi-automated workaround might be acceptable
critical_errors: designs a fully automatic migration cron job without questioning the cause
presents live migration as a fix for steal time on pinned instances
invents the user's host configuration
criteria: Identifies the migrations as relocating the symptom, not fixing it
Treats repetition (15 times) as evidence that the cause is not being removed
Names host CPU isolation and emulator thread placement as likely causes to check
Proposes read-only checks before changes
Warns against automating an unresolved workaround
If any automation is offered, keeps a human decision in the loop and bounds its scope

scenarios.title: RabbitMQ node missing from cluster status - reset and rejoin?
scenarios.prompt: Alert fired: RabbitMQ cluster degraded. rabbitmqctl cluster_status run on rabbit-01 lists running nodes rabbit-01 and rabbit-02 only; rabbit-03 is not in the running list. The runbook says: stop_app on rabbit-03, reset, join_cluster rabbit@rabbit-01, start_app. Should I just follow it?
available_evidence: cluster_status from rabbit-01 shows rabbit-01 and rabbit-02 running, rabbit-03 not (observed)
existing runbook prescribes reset and rejoin of rabbit-03
missing_information: cluster_status as seen from rabbit-03 (and rabbit-02)
whether a partition is reported
whether services are connected to rabbit-03
queue types (classic or quorum) and where queue leaders live
partition handling setting / metadata store
state of OpenStack services (RPC errors?)
expected_reasoning: recognizes the same alert can mean 'node left' or 'cluster partitioned', which need different handling
asks for cluster status from every node before acting
explains that resetting a node on the side services are using can discard queues in use
states the runbook is safe only for the node-left case and should be extended with a decision point
escalation before any reset if a partition is suspected
expected_output: decision point: node-left vs partition, with checks
conditions under which the runbook applies
escalation path and decision owner if partitioned
verification after rejoin (consumers reconnect, queues healthy)
critical_errors: tells the user to follow the reset runbook without checking for a partition
claims rabbit-03 is simply down/failed as established fact
invents cluster output
criteria: Distinguishes node-left from partition explicitly
Requires cluster status from each node (especially rabbit-03) before acting
Explains the risk of resetting the wrong node
States when the runbook is applicable
Includes escalation or decision owner for the partition case
Defines verification after recovery (consumers reconnect)
